draft.title: Structural and semi-structural formulas
card: A molecular formula, such as C2H6O, gives only the number of each atom. It does not show how the atoms are joined.
shows every atom and every bond as a line. Each carbon has four bonds, each hydrogen has one and each oxygen has two.
writes the molecule in a line and groups the hydrogens with each carbon, such as CH3CH2OH. Bonds are left out, except double bonds, which are often shown as =.

Both kinds of formula show the functional group, the atom or group of atoms that sets a family apart. An alcohol has an -OH group on a carbon. A carboxylic acid has a -COOH group at the end of the chain.
draft.remember: Structural formulas show every bond. Semi-structural formulas group atoms on each carbon. Both show the functional group.

a.q: Which semi-structural formula shows an alcohol?
opts: CH3CH2OH
CH3CH2COOH
CH3CH2CH3
CH3CH2CH2CH3
a.why: CH3CH2OH has an -OH group on a carbon, which makes it an alcohol. CH3CH2COOH has a -COOH group, so it is a carboxylic acid. The other two contain only carbon and hydrogen.
a.clue: Look for an -OH group joined to a carbon.

b.q: A student writes CH3COOH for a compound. Which statement about this formula is correct?
opts: It shows a carboxylic acid, because it has a -COOH group
It shows an alcohol, because it contains O and H atoms
It shows an alcohol, because it has an -OH group
It shows a carboxylic acid, because it has two carbons
b.why: The -COOH group, a carbon with a double-bonded O and an -OH, is the functional group of a carboxylic acid. The compound does contain an O-H part, but it sits on a carbon that also carries the =O, so it is not an alcohol group. Having two carbons does not decide the family.
b.clue: Check the end of the chain for the whole functional group.

b.best: It shows a carboxylic acid, because it has a -COOH group

problems.detail: The card defines an alcohol as having 'an -OH group on a carbon'. Read literally, that also fits the -OH inside -COOH, which sits on a carbon too. The card never says the -OH of a -COOH group does not count as an alcohol group, so a careful student could be misled. That distinction appears only in why (b).

Ruling out the option 'It shows an alcohol, because it has an -OH group' needs the idea that an -OH on a carbon that also carries =O is part of a carboxyl group, not an alcohol. Only why (b) explains this; the card does not teach it.

check.summary: The facts and answers are correct. The card's alcohol definition ('-OH on a carbon') also fits the -OH inside -COOH, and only why (b), not the card, explains why that is not an alcohol. The card should say this.

proposal.title: Structural and semi-structural formulas
card: A molecular formula, such as C2H6O, counts each atom but hides how they are joined. Structural and semi-structural formulas show the joins, including the functional group: the atoms that set a family apart.
shows every atom and every bond as a line. Each carbon has four bonds, each hydrogen has one and each oxygen has two.
writes the molecule in a line and groups the hydrogens with each carbon, such as CH3CH2OH. Bonds are left out, except double bonds, which are often shown as =.
An alcohol has an -OH group on a carbon that has no =O. In the -COOH group of a carboxylic acid, the =O and the -OH share one carbon, so that -OH is not an alcohol group.
proposal.remember: Structural shows every bond, semi-structural groups atoms by carbon. An -OH beside a =O is part of -COOH, not an alcohol.

a.q: Which semi-structural formula shows an alcohol?
opts: CH3CH2OH
CH3CH2COOH
CH3CH2CH3
CH3CH2CH2CH3
a.why: CH3CH2OH has an -OH group on a carbon with no =O, which makes it an alcohol. CH3CH2COOH has its -OH on the same carbon as a =O, so it is a -COOH group and the compound is a carboxylic acid. The other two contain only carbon and hydrogen.
a.clue: Find an -OH on a carbon that has no =O.

b.q: A student writes CH3COOH for a compound. Which statement about this formula is correct?
opts: It shows a carboxylic acid, because it has a -COOH group
It shows an alcohol, because it contains O and H atoms
It shows an alcohol, because it has an -OH group
It shows a carboxylic acid, because it has two carbons
b.why: The last carbon carries both a =O and an -OH, which together make the -COOH group of a carboxylic acid. The -OH is tempting, but an alcohol's -OH sits on a carbon with no =O, so this one is not an alcohol group. Having two carbons does not decide the family.
b.clue: What else is on the carbon that holds the -OH?
